gen_risks.description: Escalating insecurity and conflict may halt field activities, limit beneficiary access and endanger staff.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement security SOPs, use remote delivery tools, partner with NGOs in safe zones, and activate contingency plans for high‑risk areas.
gen_risks.evidence: Annex 3 describes security risk levels (green, yellow, red) and adaptations such as suspending activities or using remote methods.

gen_risks.description: Procurement processes may be delayed by administrative routines and limited bidder competition in fragile regions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit a dedicated procurement specialist, develop a detailed procurement section in the PIM, and fast‑track procedures with World Bank oversight.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement risk rated Substantial; mitigation includes hiring specialist and preparing PIM with clear procedures (p.83‑85).

gen_risks.description: The new Project Implementation Unit lacks experienced financial management staff and systems, raising fiduciary risk.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit qualified FM staff, install accounting software, adopt a comprehensive FM manual, and secure external auditor and internal audit arrangements.
gen_risks.evidence: FM assessment finds no FM staff, procedures, or software; mitigation measures listed (p.82).

gen_risks.description: Gender‑based violence and SEA/SH incidents could affect beneficiaries and damage project reputation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement SEA/SH Action Plan, train staff on code of conduct, establish confidential grievance mechanism with referral pathways for survivors.
gen_risks.evidence: SEA/SH risk assessed as Substantial; mitigation includes action plan and grievance mechanism (p.87‑89).

gen_risks.description: Interoperability of the RSU with other databases may expose personal data to breaches or non‑compliance with data protection laws.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply national data‑protection authority guidelines, enforce strict access controls, conduct regular security audits, and use permissioned APIs.
gen_risks.evidence: Subcomponent 2.2 requires data‑protection compliance and support from ANSSI and CIL (p.34‑36).

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related shocks (droughts, floods) could reduce the effectiveness of economic inclusion activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate‑smart agriculture, diversify livelihoods, and use early warning systems to adjust interventions promptly.
gen_risks.evidence: Section on climate change impacts and adaptation measures in Component 1 and 2 (p.21‑27).

gen_risks.description: Construction of warehouses may cause water and soil pollution from solid and liquid waste.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and enforce waste‑management plans, monitor site runoff, and apply pollution‑prevention standards per ESS 3.
gen_risks.evidence: E&S risks include water and soil pollution at construction sites (p.87).

gen_risks.description: Key PIU positions (GBV specialist, security specialist, external auditor) may not be filled on time, weakening oversight.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set recruitment timelines in the legal covenants, monitor progress monthly, and use interim consultants if delays occur.
gen_risks.evidence: Legal covenants require staffing within 3‑6 months of effectiveness (FA Schedule 2 sections).

gen_risks.description: Targeting errors could exclude vulnerable groups (women, youth, persons with disabilities) from benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply gender‑sensitive proxy means test, conduct community validation, and monitor exclusion indicators through BOMS.
gen_risks.evidence: Beneficiary selection uses RSU with gender‑sensitive features and community validation (p.24‑25).

gen_risks.description: Fragmented coordination among ministries may lead to duplication and inefficiency.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish inter‑ministerial coordination mechanism, regular joint planning meetings, and a shared MIS for data exchange.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 58‑59 stresses need for coordination and mentions inter‑ministerial mechanisms (p.58‑59).

gen_risks.description: Limited field monitoring due to security constraints could reduce data quality and timely issue detection.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize GEMS, phone‑based PDM, and remote verification; train local partners for on‑the‑ground data collection.
gen_risks.evidence: Monitoring plan includes remote tools like GEMS and phone‑based PDM for insecure areas (p.67‑68).

gen_risks.description: Currency fluctuations between EUR, USD and XOF may affect budgeting and disbursement amounts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include a modest contingency buffer in the budget and regularly review exchange rates for adjustments.
gen_risks.evidence: Exchange rate provided (EUR 0.8536 per USD) and financing in both currencies (p.1‑2).

gen_risks.description: CERC activation may be delayed if Emergency Action Plans are not approved in time.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare CERC Manual and EAP before effectiveness, obtain Bank approval early, and conduct mock activation drills.
gen_risks.evidence: CERC requires manual, EAP and compliance with ESCP before activation (p.53).

gen_risks.description: Grievance Redress Mechanism may not handle SEA/SH complaints effectively, leading to reputational damage.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate SEA/SH protocols into GRM, train staff on handling cases, and ensure referral pathways to specialized services.
gen_risks.evidence: GRM will include SEA/SH procedures and referral pathways (p.87‑89).

gen_risks.description: Procurement fraud or corruption could arise despite safeguards, jeopardizing project funds.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply World Bank anti‑corruption guidelines, conduct regular audits by ASCELC, and enforce transparent procurement documentation in STEP.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement follows World Bank regulations and anti‑corruption guidelines (p.83‑84).

gen_risks.description: MFIs may lack capacity to process productive grants and financial education for beneficiaries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide capacity‑building workshops for MFIs, establish clear grant disbursement procedures, and monitor service delivery performance.
gen_risks.evidence: MFIs will receive productive grants and provide financial education (p.66‑67).

gen_risks.description: Roll‑out of the Unique Social Registry may miss target coverage, delaying identification of poor households.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set phased rollout milestones, allocate additional field teams for hard‑to‑reach areas, and monitor registration progress monthly.
gen_risks.evidence: RSU aims to cover 800,000 households; rollout depends on poverty, security, climate risk (p.32‑33).

gen_risks.description: Limited mobile network coverage could hinder digital payment platform (Faso Arzeka) usage by beneficiaries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct network feasibility study, use hybrid cash‑plus‑mobile options, and partner with telecoms to expand coverage where needed.
gen_risks.evidence: Payment platform adaptation mentions assessing mobile network coverage and cash points (p.36‑38).

gen_risks.description: Inadequate logistics (vehicles, warehouses) may prevent timely shock response deliveries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Procure vehicles and construct warehouses per the logistics plan, monitor stock levels, and establish contingency stock buffers.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 3.1 funds procurement of 48 vehicles and 28 warehouses for shock response (p.40‑41).

gen_risks.description: High staff turnover or insufficient training could weaken project implementation capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement staff retention incentives, continuous capacity‑building programs, and document standard operating procedures for knowledge transfer.
gen_risks.evidence: PIU will recruit and train staff across multiple specialties; past experience noted (p.63‑64).

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk is assessed to be Substantial. The uncertain political and governance context provides a challenge to long-term development policy. Adaptive social protection systems are still nascent and will require continued political commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The team, guided by the management, will continue its high-level policy dialogue at central and decentralized levels and ensure continuous advocacy and communication.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is assessed to be Substantial. Fiscal space remains constrained by elevated security spending and tighter financing conditions, which increase the risk of reduced budget allocations and delayed counterpart funding for new priorities and reforms, including social protection and the PAMPV. Macroeconomic risks also arise from exogenous factors, including current conflict in the Middle East which can result in a surge in oil prices and put inflationary pressure.
gt_risks.mitigation: Other programs such as the International Monetary Fund program and the World Bank's technical assistance on tax expenditure under the Sustainable Development Finance Policy can help expand fiscal space, partially mitigating these risks.

gt_risks.description: Sector strategy and policies risks are considered to be Substantial. Sectoral strategies and policies remain nascent, and the Government's budget allocation to operationalize the PAMPV remains unclear. Also, sectoral decisions are at times taken abruptly and can heavily affect implementation (for example, the suspension of cash transfers in 2023 led to an increased focus on economic inclusion, and the newly emerged priority of the CONASUR/IDPs led to the revision of the fiche de projet of this project).
gt_risks.mitigation: In parallel with high-level policy dialogue, the project supports strategic communications, adopts an agile approach, and provides technical assistance to promote evidence-based decision-making (with support from SASPP, the Social Protection Response MDTF, and the State and Peacebuilding Fund).

gt_risks.description: Overall fiduciary risks are considered as Substantial, as described in section IV.B and annex 2, based on financial assessment and procurement assessment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project preparation fund (Grant Facility for Project Preparation) has been used not only to prepare mitigation measures to address these risks but will also elevate the project readiness (for example, effectiveness-linked actions including FM and procurement staffing and initiating the procurement packages for the first 18-months' implementation priorities) to improve the project performance.

gt_risks.description: Other risks related to insecurity are rated as High. The deteriorating and volatile security situation—particularly in regions with high poverty, displacement, and food insecurity that are project intervention areas—will likely be an important risk. The project will also address other risks related to protection of personal data: for Component 2 on social registry and interoperability, activities will be guided by the Information System Security Policy (ISSP) document developed by the ANSSI, to ensure confidentiality of households registered in the RSU.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project activities will be adjusted based on the security situation (see annex 3), and the PIU will be also staffed with a security specialist and a security management plan will be developed. To remain engaged, the project will also rely on remote delivery/monitoring, partnering with local representation (NGOs, UN agencies). The ST-RSU will conduct capacity-building activities, including training sessions and awareness campaigns, to strengthen users' ability to manage and protect households' personal data.
